seo_description: A continuous free product system whose maximal tensor core generates only a proper subsystem. Read Alec Kriebel’s preprint, proof, and source materials.
plain_language: A product system describes how mathematical spaces for shorter time intervals combine into a space for a longer interval. There are different ways to combine them. Tensor products impose one kind of ordering; free products allow a richer collection of alternating combinations.

The question is whether the largest tensor subsystem inside a free product system always contains enough information to rebuild the whole free system. This paper constructs an example where it does not. Its tensor core generates all the finite-word sectors, but the full system also contains orthogonal sectors made from infinite words. Taking limits of the finite-word sectors cannot reach those extra sectors.
The construction retains separable Hilbert spaces and proves a specified continuous dependence on time, including at time zero. The obstruction therefore persists beyond a purely algebraic example.
central_result: There exists an associative pointed free product system E of separable complex Hilbert spaces such that, at every positive time t, its maximal ordered tensor subsystem F is the time-ordered finite-word Fock system, the closed free subsystem generated by F is the full finite-word Fock system K, and K_t is a proper subspace of E_t. A nonzero grade-ω sector witnesses the strict inclusion.
why_it_matters: The example gives a negative answer in the scalar case to the universal tensor-core generation question stated by Michael Skeide in 2009: the largest tensor subsystem need not generate the entire free product system.
limits: The theorem uses the explicit continuous Hilbert-field convention stated in the paper. It does not assert every possible stronger regularity axiom.
It does not answer the separate adapted-cocycle or forward tensor-recovery questions, or classify free product systems.
The argument is analytic. Finite computational checks do not certify the infinite-dimensional claims.
This is an unrefereed preprint. The historical comparison is bounded and does not establish worldwide firstness.

collaboration: I welcome substantive collaboration on an independent mathematical review of the construction, particularly its measure-class factorization and continuity arguments, or on developing a journal submission. Authorship would reflect the contributions made to that work.
followup_rationale: None recommended. Stronger regularity, classification, or adapted-cocycle questions are broad or pre-existing, and this bounded review does not establish a precise new extension with a compelling publication case. Varying the ordinal cutoff would be a routine extension without a demonstrated additional payoff.
proof_summary: A recoverable Gaussian mixture gives a sigma-finite measure class on convergent infinite sequences that is preserved under finite-prefix absorption.
Words of ordinal length below ω² split at a time cut into finitely many monochromatic runs, producing associative pointed free-product unitaries and the specified continuity structure.
Intersecting ordered tensor ranges leaves decreasing finite words. Their free hull contains exactly finite words, while a positive finite-measure grade-ω set supplies a nonzero orthogonal remainder.
title: A continuous free product system not generated by its tensor core
author: Alec Kriebel
abstract_tex:
We construct an associative pointed free product system of separable complex
Hilbert spaces whose maximal ordered tensor subsystem does not generate the
whole free system. Its tensor core is the time-ordered finite-word Fock system,
and the closed free subsystem generated by that core is precisely the full
finite-word Fock system. The ambient system has, in addition, nonzero orthogonal
sectors of words of ordinal length below $\omega^2$. A recoverable Gaussian
mixture supplies a sigma-finite measure class invariant under finite-prefix
absorption. Finite monochromatic-run charts turn concatenation into the free
product structure. We prove separability, an explicit continuous Hilbert-field
structure including time zero, and continuity of the full structural maps and
their inverses. This gives a negative answer, in the scalar specialization, to
the universal tensor-core generation question stated by Skeide in 2009. It does
not answer the separate adapted-cocycle or forward tensor-recovery questions.
The argument is analytic; accompanying finite computations do not certify its
infinite-dimensional assertions. This draft is unrefereed and extensively
AI-assisted.
